episode_title: Are You Governing Both Sides of AI?

real_qa.q: How does DOJ compliance program guidance address AI governance in both business and compliance functions?
real_qa.r: DOJ's compliance program guidance already asks how a company governs AI in both its business and its compliance program, and what baseline of human decision-making it uses to judge the tools. It also asks whether compliance has technology comparable to the business.
real_qa.requete: DOJ compliance program AI governance guidance

real_qa.q: What OFAC framework applies to AI screening tools and which companies faced penalties for weak matching results?
real_qa.r: OFAC's 2019 framework covers screening tools. Amazon and Payoneer paid penalties for weak matching results.
real_qa.requete: OFAC 2019 framework AI screening Amazon Payoneer penalties

real_qa.q: What are the two tracks in an integrated AI compliance program?
real_qa.r: Track one uses AI to strengthen compliance in screening, monitoring, third-party diligence, hotline triage, and investigations. Track two governs the risk AI creates, from shadow AI and data leakage to unverified output, bias, and deliberate misuse.
real_qa.requete: two tracks AI compliance program governance

real_qa.q: Why is AI governance failing in most companies according to current compliance structures?
real_qa.r: Most companies have AI in two different rooms: innovation buys the tools, compliance writes the policy, and nobody connects. AI isn't a separate program but flows through every element of the one you already have.

transcript_full: Most companies have AI in two different rooms. Innovation buys the tools, compliance writes the policy. Nobody connects. Here's the core idea. There are two tracks in one program. Track one, use AI to strengthen compliance in screening, monitoring, third-party diligence, hotline triage, and investigations. Track two, govern the risk AI creates, from shadow AI and data leakage to unverified output, bias, and deliberate misuse. And you don't have to wait for an AI-specific statute. DOJ's compliance program guidance already asks how a company governs AI in both its business and its compliance program, and what baseline of human decision-making it uses to judge the tools. It also asks whether compliance has technology comparable to the business. OFAC's 2019 framework covers your screening tools, too, and Amazon and Payoneer pay penalties for weak matching results. AI isn't a separate program. It flows through every element of the one you already have. If ethics and compliance is your passion, we need to talk. find me at volkofflaw.com.
